In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic valuation of environmental resources, and in particular, the economic valuation of recreational resources.
the evaluation of the recreational value of the Idro Lake and the estimation of the economic benefits deriving for its recreational uses.

the following issues: i) the evaluation of the value of recreational uses of the Idro Lake, ii) the evaluation of a possible change in the quality of these uses, and iii) the estimation of the economic benefits deriving both from current recreational demand and from the hypothetical one obtained considering a “improved quality”.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if the lake is not cleaned up, its recreational use is not economically sustainable.
, in the Idro Lake, recreational uses have a high economic value, and that the increase of the quality of the water would lead to an increase of the economic value of recreational uses.

, in the case of the Idro Lake, the economic value of recreational use of water is higher than the value of competitive uses, but the clean up costs are higher than the economic benefits deriving by the recreational use of water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Idro Lake, which is currently in a critical condition, should not be considered as a mere reservoir for productive uses, but as a resource having a recreational value.
the Idro Lake has an economic value for recreational uses that is higher than its economic value for productive uses, and that the clean up of the lake is an economically viable option.

the Idro Lake is a valuable resource that needs to be protected, but also that its recreational use is an important source of economic benefits that should be taken into account in any policy aimed at improving the lake’s water quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stated preference and revealed preference approaches can be fruitfully combined to estimate the economic value of environmental resources having a recreational use.
the combined approach is able to provide more reliable estimates than the RP or the SP approach alone.
, in order to evaluate environmental resources, a combination of SP and RP methods should be considered, in order to overcome the limits of both approaches.
